transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

It’s a bit embarrassing to admit, but the minute I even get near blood tests or needles, I feel an immediate wave of fear that makes me want to bolt from the clinic. I just can't seem to handle being around them anymore.
Do you have this intense fear only with blood, injections, or needles, or do you also react the same way to other things like seeing injuries, medical procedures, or fainting?

Needles, blood draws, and IVs are definitely the absolute worst, but the fear has spread to almost any medical setting or procedure, like hospitals or even getting a colonoscopy. Whenever I'm forced to stay and face those situations, I get this intense, lightheaded feeling like I'm actually going to pass out.
When you feel lightheaded in these situations, have you actually fainted or nearly fainted before, or is it mainly fear and dizziness without passing out?

I’ve never actually fainted completely, but I’ve come incredibly close. When I'm sitting in that chair, I get so dizzy and lightheaded that I have to white-knuckle the armrests just to stay upright. It's this overwhelming wave of dread where I feel like I'm right on the edge of blacking out.

Do you feel this same intense fear and near-fainting reaction in any other specific situations, such as heights, flying, closed spaces, or being in public, or is it mainly limited to blood, needles, and medical procedures?

No, it's strictly limited to needles, blood, and medical settings. Things like heights, flying, or closed spaces don't bother me at all. This intense panic and feeling like I'm going to pass out only happens when I'm dealing with medical procedures.
Do you now avoid medical appointments, blood tests, or procedures because of this fear, or do you go only with a lot of distress?

I actually do both. I go out of my way to avoid them by rescheduling my own appointments and just dropping my sister off at the curb, but if I absolutely have to stay, I end up white-knuckling the chair and staring at the floor in absolute dread.
Do you feel the same intense fear and urge to avoid with other specific things, like animals, storms, flying, or heights, or is it only blood, needles, and medical procedures?

It is strictly limited to blood, needles, and medical settings. Other common fears like animals, storms, or heights don't bother me at all. It's only the medical stuff that triggers this kind of panic and dread.
When you are facing blood, needles, or medical procedures, do you mainly feel fear of the pain/injury itself, or do you also get a sudden drop in heart rate, nausea, or actually faint?

It is honestly a bit of both. I have this intense fear that the needle is going to stab straight through my arm, but physically, my heart pounds rapidly, my chest tightens, and my hands get sweaty. I also get extremely lightheaded, like I'm about to pass out, even though I've never actually fainted completely.
When you are around blood, needles, or medical procedures, is the main fear the pain or injury itself, or is it more the feeling of fainting/passing out?

It’s actually a combination of both. I have this intense fear of the needle itself, feeling like it’s going to stab straight through my arm, but I also get incredibly lightheaded and dizzy, like I'm going to pass out the entire time I'm trying to endure it.
When you’re facing blood, needles, or medical procedures, is your main fear more about fainting/passing out, or more about the pain/injury from the needle itself?

It’s really a combination of both. I have this intense fear of the needle stabbing straight through my arm, but when I'm forced to sit through it, I also feel incredibly lightheaded and constantly worry that I'm going to pass out.
Have you ever actually fainted or lost consciousness during a blood draw, injection, or other medical procedure?

No, I have never actually fainted or lost consciousness during any of those procedures. However, the entire time I am forced to endure them, I constantly feel extremely lightheaded and like I am right on the verge of passing out.
Have you ever had this same intense fear or near-fainting feeling in any other situations, or is it only when you see blood, needles, or medical procedures?

No, this intense fear and the feeling of nearly passing out are strictly limited to needles, blood draws, IVs, and medical settings. I don't experience this kind of panic or physical reaction in any other area of my life. Outside of these medical situations, I'm completely fine.
When you’re exposed to blood, needles, or medical procedures, do you actually faint or lose consciousness, or is it mainly intense fear and feeling like you might pass out without fully fainting?

I have never actually fainted or lost consciousness. It is just an intense feeling like I might pass out, which forces me to grip the chair and white-knuckle my way through the procedure while staring at the floor.
When you think about blood, needles, or medical procedures, is your main fear more about actually fainting or passing out, or more about the pain/injury from the needle or blood itself?

It is actually a mix of both. I have this intense fear of the needle itself, feeling like it's going to stab straight through my arm. But when I'm forced to endure the procedure, I end up white-knuckling the chair and feeling like I am going to pass out the entire time.
When you are exposed to blood or needles, do you feel your heart slow down, your blood pressure drop, or get nauseated right before the lightheadedness, or is it mainly a rapid heartbeat and panic?

When the fear first hits, it is definitely a rapid, pounding heartbeat, chest tightness, and sweaty hands. However, if I am forced to stay and actually endure the procedure, that's when I get that really strong feeling like I might pass out.

When you start feeling lightheaded around blood or needles, do you ever actually see your vision narrow, feel nauseated, or notice your heart slowing down right before it happens? Or is it mostly a rapid heartbeat and panic from the start?

It is definitely a rapid, pounding heartbeat and intense panic right from the start, along with chest tightness and sweaty hands. I don't really notice my heart slowing down or nausea, but when I'm forced to stay, that's when I get that strong sensation like I might pass out while white-knuckling through the procedure.
When you are around blood or needles, do you ever actually faint, or do you mainly feel panic and fear of passing out without losing consciousness?

I have never actually fainted or lost consciousness, but I get an overwhelming sensation like I might pass out the entire time. To get through it, I end up gripping the chair, staring at the floor, and white-knuckling it while my heart pounds, my chest tightens, and my hands get sweaty.
Do you also get this fear and near-fainting feeling when you see other people’s blood or injuries, or only when you are the one getting needles or medical procedures?

I actually get it in both situations; in fact, watching my sister get her IV infusion two years ago is what made this fear so much worse, which is why I now avoid going into her appointments with her. I experience the exact same intense fear and near-fainting feeling whether it is happening to me during my own blood tests, or if I have to watch or think about someone else going through a medical procedure.
Do you get this same fear or near-fainting feeling only with blood, needles, and medical procedures, or also with other specific things like seeing injuries, cuts, or accidents?

It is really just clinical things like needles, blood draws, IVs, and medical environments that trigger this reaction. While I don't particularly like seeing general injuries, cuts, or accidents, they don't cause the same overwhelming panic and physical response that medical procedures do.
When you are around blood or needles, do you ever feel more faint, nauseated, or like your heart slows down right before it happens, or is it mainly a fast heartbeat and panic the whole time?

It is actually a mix of both. My heart starts pounding fast, my chest tightens, and my hands sweat with panic as soon as I walk into the clinic. But if I have to sit through the procedure, that's when I also feel incredibly lightheaded and like I might pass out the entire time.
When you are exposed to blood, needles, or medical procedures, do you ever actually faint or lose consciousness, or do you mainly feel intense fear and lightheadedness without fully passing out?

I have never actually fainted or lost consciousness, but I feel extremely close to it. The entire time, I experience intense fear with my heart pounding, and I have to white-knuckle the chair just to get through it, feeling like I might pass out at any second.
When you face blood, needles, or medical procedures, do you ever feel faint because of a sudden drop in energy or nausea, or is it mainly a panic reaction with a racing heart and fear from the start?

It’s definitely a combination of both reactions. When I first encounter the situation, I get an immediate panic response with my heart pounding, my chest tightening, and my hands sweating. But if I actually have to stay and endure the procedure, that's when I get extremely lightheaded and feel like I might pass out.
When you feel lightheaded around blood or needles, do you ever actually faint after the initial panic settles, or is it always just a fear of passing out without losing consciousness?

I've never actually fainted or lost consciousness, even after the initial panic. Instead, I experience this intense lightheadedness where I feel like I'm constantly on the verge of passing out, forcing me to grip the chair and white-knuckle it until the procedure is finally over.
When you see blood or needles, do you ever get a brief drop in heart rate, nausea, or a fainting spell after the initial panic, or is it mainly a fast heartbeat and fear without those symptoms?

It definitely starts with a fast, pounding heartbeat, sweating, and intense panic when I first encounter the situation. However, if I am forced to stay and endure it, I end up gripping the chair and feeling like I might actually pass out the whole time. I don't really experience nausea or a drop in my heart rate that I've noticed.

When you are in these medical situations, do you ever actually faint or feel nauseated/see your vision go dark right before it happens, or is it mainly a fast heartbeat and panic with only a feeling that you might pass out?

It is definitely the fast heartbeat, chest tightness, sweaty hands, and panic, along with that strong feeling that I might pass out while I'm white-knuckling through it. I don't actually faint, and I have never lost my vision or felt nauseated. It is just that overwhelming sensation of lightheadedness and dread.
Would you say the fear is mainly about blood, injections, or needles themselves, or is it more about any medical procedure or setting even when there is no blood or needle involved?

The core of my fear is definitely about needles, shots, and IVs—I constantly feel like they are going to stab straight through my arm. However, it has generalized so much now that just walking into a hospital or facing other procedures like a colonoscopy triggers my anxiety and avoidance, even if a needle isn't immediately present.

When you are in a medical setting without any needles or blood present, like sitting in a waiting room or seeing a doctor for a non-procedure visit, do you still get the same intense fear and urge to escape?

Yes, absolutely. Just walking through the hospital doors, sitting in the waiting room, or hearing staff talk about potential blood work makes my chest tighten and my heart pound with that same immediate urge to escape. It’s actually why I've resorted to dropping my sister off at the curb instead of walking inside with her, just to avoid being in that environment.
When you are in a medical setting without any needles or blood present, like a waiting room or a routine doctor visit, do you still get the same intense fear and urge to escape?

Yes, definitely. Even if there's no needle in sight, just walking through the hospital doors or sitting in the waiting area triggers that same intense panic and pounding chest. That's why I've started dropping my sister off at the curb instead of going inside with her, because the urge to run away is just too strong.
When you are in a medical setting without any needles or blood present, like a waiting room or routine doctor visit, do you still get the same intense fear and urge to escape?

Yes, absolutely. Just walking through those clinic doors or hearing the staff talk about medical stuff makes my chest tighten and my heart pound, even before any needles are in sight. That's why I've resorted to dropping my sister off at the curb, just to avoid having to step foot inside the building.

Is your fear and urge to escape mainly triggered by blood, needles, and medical procedures, or do you also get the same reaction in other situations like seeing injuries, accidents, or even just thinking about them?

It is strictly triggered by needles, blood tests, IVs, and being in medical environments like hospital clinics. I don't get this intense reaction from general injuries or accidents; it is really about those specific medical procedures involving needles and tubes in my arm.
When you feel this fear, is it only triggered by blood, injections, and medical procedures, or do you also react strongly to other things like seeing injuries, accidents, or wounds?

It is strictly the needles, shots, and clinical procedures themselves that trigger my panic. I don't really experience this extreme fear with general injuries, wounds, or accidents outside of a medical setting. It's the clinical environment and the needles that cause me to panic.
